causes.title: Huang's reinstatement
causes.text: The main driver was one board decision. On Monday, Nov 23, Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director. Huang had resigned just 11 days earlier, following allegations of affairs, according to the Motley Fool. The shares surged 31.48% that day, adding about $950 billion in market value, TheStreet reported. The board said it voted after discussions with Huang and input from senior levels of the US government. It added that it is confident his reinstatement poses no national security risk. The statement also said the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion, and that Nvidia will keep cooperating with government investigations and inquiries. So the CEO question closed while others stayed open. Citi's Atif Malik framed it this way: the reinstatement removes the key overhang created by the CEO transition. The link to the week is direct. Monday's jump was larger than the full-week gain of 19.9%, and Friday added only about 0.8%. Most of the week's move was this single day.

causes.title: Analysts reverse course
causes.text: Several analysts who had stepped back returned on Monday. StoneX's Cody Acree upgraded Nvidia to Buy from Hold with a $270 target. That is $65 below his prior $335 estimate, which StoneX halted after Huang resigned, TheStreet noted. Oppenheimer's Rick Schafer upgraded to Outperform with a $250 target. Melius Research's Ben Reitzes upgraded to Buy and raised his target to $220 from $185. Citi's Atif Malik raised his target to $240 from $225. Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon upgraded the stock back to Outperform, though he also called the board's on-again-off-again response clown-like. Yorkville's Dan Ives said the stock should be valued at $300 with Huang back. According to LSEG data cited by CNBC, 48 of 65 analysts covering Nvidia rated it Buy or Strong Buy. The notes landed on the same day as the 31.48% jump. They reinforced the move rather than preceded it, and the lower StoneX target shows the upgrades came with some caution.

causes.title: Market-wide rebound
causes.text: Nvidia did not rise alone. The week before, the S&P 500 fell 8.61%, its largest weekly drop since April 4, 2025. Monday's rebound was broad. The Nasdaq closed up 6.51%, the S&P 500 rose 4.73% and the Dow gained 3.01%, according to Wallstreetcn via Longbridge, which tied the move to Huang's return. Wednesday gave some back. October PCE inflation was 3.8%, matching forecasts, but core PCE of 3.3% topped the 3.2% forecast. By 9:40 a.m. ET, QQQ was down 4.17%. Polymarket priced a quarter-point Fed hike for December at 93%. Friday's shortened session helped. The Nasdaq climbed 2.31% to 24,129.50 as chipmakers led, and Marvell jumped 7.34% to $140.54. For the week, the S&P 500 rose 5.6% and the Nasdaq rose 6.68%. Nvidia's 19.9% gain was well above both, so the stock moved with the market and then went further.

after_causes.title: Every stock rose
after_causes.text: All eight tracked stocks finished the week higher. Nvidia led at +19.9%, followed by Tesla at +15.7% and Meta at +12.2%. Those three beat the Nasdaq-100's +6.8%. Apple rose +4.7% and closed at its 52-week high. Alphabet gained +3.6%, Amazon +3.0%, Broadcom +2.6% and Microsoft +1.7%. Amazon closed up +4.0% on Friday, after Adobe said Thanksgiving Day online spending hit $7.1 billion. The month still looks rough for several names. Nvidia is −30.1% over about a month and Microsoft is −7.2%.

The board said its own committee investigation will proceed to conclusion, and Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi notes that Justice Department and SEC investigations into alleged chip smuggling remain. New detail from any of these would give the bear case more to work with. A quiet outcome would leave the bull argument on earnings and valuation, such as 17 times forward estimates, as the main one. causes.title: Huang's reinstatement
causes.text: The main company-specific driver was one board decision. On Monday, Nov 23, Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director. Huang had resigned just 11 days earlier, following allegations of affairs, according to the Motley Fool. The shares surged 31.48% that day, adding about $950 billion in market value, TheStreet reported. The board said it voted after discussions with Huang and input from senior levels of the US government. It added that it is confident his reinstatement poses no national security risk. The statement also said the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion, and that Nvidia will keep cooperating with government investigations and inquiries. So the CEO question closed while others stayed open. Citi's Atif Malik framed it this way: the reinstatement removes the key overhang created by the CEO transition. The weekly numbers need care. Monday's jump was larger than the full-week gain of 19.9%, so the other days combined netted lower, even though Friday added about 0.8%.

causes.title: Analysts reverse course
causes.text: Analysts changed their calls after Huang's return. StoneX's Cody Acree upgraded Nvidia to Buy from Hold on Nov 23 with a $270 target. That is $65 below his prior $335 estimate, which StoneX halted after Huang resigned. TheStreet's headline called that a surprising catch. Oppenheimer's Rick Schafer upgraded to Outperform with a $250 target. Melius Research's Ben Reitzes upgraded to Buy and raised his target to $220 from $185. Citi's Atif Malik raised his target to $240 from $225. Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon upgraded the stock back to Outperform, though he also called the board's on-again-off-again response clown-like. Yorkville's Dan Ives said the stock should be valued at $300 with Huang back. According to LSEG data cited by CNBC, 48 of 65 analysts covering Nvidia rated its shares Buy or Strong Buy. The sources do not settle whether the notes pushed the price or followed it.

causes.title: Market-wide rebound
causes.text: Nvidia did not rise alone. The week before, the S&P 500 fell 8.61%, its largest weekly drop since April 4, 2025. Monday's rebound was broad. The Nasdaq closed up 6.51%, the S&P 500 rose 4.73% and the Dow gained 3.01%, according to Wallstreetcn via Longbridge, which tied the move to Huang's return. Wednesday gave some back. October PCE inflation was 3.8%, matching forecasts, but core PCE of 3.3% topped the 3.2% forecast. By 9:40 a.m. ET, QQQ was down 4.17%. Polymarket priced a quarter-point Fed hike for December at 93%. Friday's shortened session helped. The Nasdaq climbed 2.31% to 24,129.50 as chipmakers led, and Marvell jumped 7.34% to $140.54. For the week, the S&P 500 rose 5.6% and the Nasdaq rose 6.68%. Nvidia's 19.9% gain was well above both, so the stock moved with the market and then went further.

after_causes.title: Every stock rose
after_causes.text: All eight tracked stocks finished the week higher. Nvidia led at +19.9%, followed by Tesla at +15.7% and Meta at +12.2%. Those three beat the Nasdaq-100's +6.8%. Apple rose +4.7% and closed at its yearly high. Alphabet gained +3.6%, Amazon +3.0%, Broadcom +2.6% and Microsoft +1.7%. Amazon closed up +4.0% on Friday. By mid-morning its shares were up 2.96%, as Adobe reported $7.1 billion in Thanksgiving Day online spending. The month still looks rough for several names. Nvidia is −30.1% over about a month and Microsoft is −7.2%.
